question.text: A faulty thermometer reads <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> in melting ice and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>95</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> in steam. The correct temperature on absolute scale will be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> when the faulty thermometer reads <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>41</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>.

solution.text:
As per working of thermometers, X-LFPUFP-LFP=constant.

Therefore, we can write

 41°-5°95°-5°=C-0°100°-0°

⇒C=3690×100=40°C=40+273 K=313 K
